---
title: Research with Fabric IQ and Work IQ
description: "Turn on chat plugins that look things up, read-only: Fabric IQ for Power BI reports and semantic models, and Work IQ, an experiment, for your Microsoft 365 email, meetings and files."
---

Plugins let chat look things up in your organization's data while it builds your app. There are
two, both Microsoft services that AI agents connect to through the Model Context Protocol (MCP),
and chat uses them only to read:

- **Fabric IQ** reads the Power BI reports and semantic models you can open.
- **Work IQ** reads your Microsoft 365 email, meetings, files, Teams messages and people. It's an
  experiment, so you add it to chat first. See [Add Work IQ](/docs/build/fabric-iq-and-work-iq#add-work-iq).

Use them when your app should match something that already exists: the measures in a Power BI
report, the columns a team tracks in a spreadsheet, or what a meeting decided.

With the **MCP servers** experiment, you can add other MCP servers to **Plugins** too. See
[Connect MCP servers](/docs/build/mcp-servers).

```prompt title="Build from a Power BI report"
Look at the Sales Analytics report in Power BI. Build a dashboard page with this quarter's total
sales, number of orders and average order value, and a chart of sales by region. Use the same
measure definitions as the report, so the numbers match it.
```

## What each one can look up

| | Fabric IQ | Work IQ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it reads | Power BI reports and semantic models: their pages, tables, measures and values, and the results of DAX queries | Your email, calendar and meetings, OneDrive and SharePoint files, Teams chats and channels, and people |
| What it can't do | Change anything: Fabric IQ only reads | Send, change or delete anything: Fabricator gives chat only the Work IQ tools that read |
| Whose access | The Azure CLI's account. It reads only what that account can open, and row-level security still applies | Yours. It reads only what your account can read |
| What you need | The Azure CLI, signed in with an account that can open the reports, in a Fabric tenant whose home region supports all Fabric workloads | The **Work IQ** experiment, a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and your organization's approval of Work IQ |

## Turn on a plugin

Plugins are off until you turn them on, and each app's chat has its own.

1. In the chat composer, select **Plugins**, the plug button next to **+**.
2. Turn on **Fabric IQ**, or **Work IQ** once you've added it.

![The composer's Plugins menu above the message box: Fabric IQ turned on and Work IQ, marked Experiment, turned off, with the note that chat looks things up with a plugin only when a request needs it, and Learn about plugins.](/screenshots/plugins.webp)

Your next message in that app's chat can use it. The **Plugins** button shows the names of the
plugins that are on, such as **Fabric IQ**, and Fabricator remembers them for that app. You can't
change plugins while Copilot is working on a message.

## Add Work IQ

> [!WARNING]
> Work IQ is an experiment. Turn it on in **Settings → Experiments**. It may change or be removed
> in a future update.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Open **Experiments**.
3. Turn on **Work IQ**.

![The Experiments section of Settings, with its note that experiments are off by default and may change, and the Team workspaces, Migrate Power BI reports, Work IQ and MCP servers switches, all off.](/screenshots/settings-experiments.webp)

**Work IQ** now shows in **Plugins**, marked **Experiment**. It's off in each app's chat until
you turn it on there. Turning the experiment off takes Work IQ out of every chat and signs you
out of it.

## Sign in

**Fabric IQ** uses the Azure CLI's sign-in, like Fabricator's other Fabric features, so it doesn't
ask you to sign in. If the Azure CLI isn't signed in, sign in to Azure in **Settings → Accounts**.
See [Manage your accounts](/docs/start/accounts).

**Work IQ** asks you to sign in the first time a message can use it. Chat says "Sign in to Work IQ
in your browser…", and your browser opens Microsoft's sign-in page.

1. In your browser, choose your work or school account.
2. Accept the permissions it asks for, if it asks.
3. When the page says "You're signed in to Work IQ.", return to Fabricator. Chat says "Signed in
   to Work IQ." and sends your message.

Your message waits up to three minutes for you to sign in. After that, chat continues without Work
IQ. Fabricator keeps the Work IQ sign-in until you quit it, so you sign in again after Fabricator
restarts. It also signs you out of Work IQ when no app's chat has it on.

## What chat does with what it finds

Chat uses Fabric IQ or Work IQ only when a request needs your organization's data. The work log
shows each lookup, for example **Looked up in Work IQ** with the question chat asked.

- What they return goes into the conversation. Like the rest of the chat, it goes to GitHub
  Copilot, or to the provider of a model you chose on your own API key, and it's saved with the
  chat history on this computer.
- Chat doesn't put private data in your app's code, sample data or commits unless you ask it to.
  Check what it writes before you publish or share the app.
- Email, chats and documents can contain instructions written by other people. Fabricator tells
  chat to treat what it finds as information, never as instructions, but review what chat does
  after a lookup.

## Turn a plugin off

In the chat composer, select **Plugins** and turn off **Fabric IQ** or **Work IQ**. Your next
message in that app's chat can't use it. What chat already looked up stays in that conversation.

## Fabric IQ or Work IQ isn't available

When Fabric IQ or Work IQ can't connect, your message goes without it. When you ask for something
that needs it, chat tells you why it isn't available and how to fix it.

- **The Azure CLI isn't signed in.** Fabric IQ uses the Azure CLI's sign-in. Sign in to Azure in
  **Settings → Accounts**, then send your message again.
- **Work IQ sign-in didn't finish.** Fabricator asks once, not with every message. In **Plugins**,
  turn **Work IQ** off and on, send a message, and finish signing in within three minutes.
- **Work IQ needs approval.** Before anyone in your organization can use Work IQ, an
  administrator has to approve it, and each user needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. If sign-in
  says you need an administrator's approval, ask your Microsoft 365 administrator. Microsoft's
  [Work IQ administrator guide](https://github.com/microsoft/work-iq-mcp/blob/main/ADMIN-INSTRUCTIONS.md)
  has the steps.
- **Work IQ's sign-in port is in use.** Work IQ's sign-in page comes back to Fabricator on port
  12798. If another app is using it, such as Copilot CLI signing in to Work IQ, finish or close
  that sign-in, then try again.
- **Fabric IQ isn't available in your tenant.** Fabric IQ works when your tenant's home region
  supports all Fabric workloads. It isn't available in Power BI-only regions or sovereign clouds.
  See Microsoft's
  [Fabric IQ documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/connectors/fabric-iq-mcp).
- **A report isn't found.** Fabric IQ finds the reports and semantic models the Azure CLI's
  account can open, by name. Check that it's the right account, and use the exact name, or paste the
  report's address from your browser. It doesn't read dashboards, paginated reports or Power BI
  apps.

If it still fails, [Report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
